text:
maria: Quick check — I opened an RFC PR yesterday about splitting service auth surface into (1) project-scoped API keys for product features and (2) ephemeral service-to-service tokens for infra flows. Wanted to surface tradeoffs before merging.

alex: Saw it, skimmed. main question: do we enforce mutual exclusion (can't have both for same service) or allow overlap?

jordan: i'd prefer allowing overlap for migration. hard block causes rollout friction. :+1:

sam: Agree with jordan. Also need to think about auditing: long-lived keys create noisy permissions. can we auto-attach metadata to API keys so we can filter by "purpose"?

maria: Proposal includes metadata fields: owner, purpose, intended-scope (org|project|service), and rotation-window. example: `{"purpose":"build-agent","scope":"project:acme/inference"}`

alex: That helps. but how do we represent RBAC ties? do we bind API keys to roles or to explicit policy documents?

maria: The RFC suggests role-binding (role_id on key) + optional inline policy for overrides. simpler for UI + audits.

security-eng: Inline policies complicate evaluation at runtime. prefer role-only + allow short-lived policy attach (ephemeral) for rare exceptions.

sam: For service auth, we should push ephemeral tokens issued by an auth broker with audience claim and optional capability claim. TTL defaults to 15m. Example issuance call:```curl -X POST https://auth.internal/issue -d '{"client_id":"ci-agent","aud":"runtime","cap":"read:kv"}'```

jordan: How about key rotation UX? ops hate having to coordinate deployments just to rotate a project API key. can we support transparent rotation (old+new overlap) and automated secret sync to dedicated pools?

infra-bot: FYI: we already have a secret-syncer prototype that can inject new keys into Dedicated pools, supports rolling update hooks. (link: https://git.internal/secret-syncer)

alex: cool. fallback behavior on mismatch — if a service sees a token with insufficient scope, should it 401 or 403? We need consistency for clients vs infra.

maria: prefer 403 for authz failures (token recognized but insufficient perms), 401 for unauthenticated/malformed tokens. Add clear error body so clients can retry with token refresh flow.

security-eng: Also add telemetry: token_type, role_id, scope_hash to logs (no raw keys). must be PII-free.

sam: one more: project vs org scoping. For multi-tenant customers we should default to project-scoped keys and only allow org keys for org-admins with explicit justification and OA approval. keep org keys audited tightly.

jordan: sounds good. i can draft a short migration plan: 1) allow overlap, 2) default new keys to project-scoped, 3) create rotate+sync tooling, 4) deprecate old long-lived org keys with 6mo notice.

maria: thanks. can someone add a small section in RFC about evaluation cost for auth checks? we need to ensure token introspection is cached to avoid QPS blowups on runtime paths.

alex: yes — add L1 cache with 1s TTL at runtime and central cache for introspection with 30s TTL. also async invalidation hooks for revocation.

security-eng: I'll drop a short checklist for compliance (KMS provenance, audit retention rules, key labeling).

maria: awesome. I'll update the RFC with these and ping again. thx all :pray:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: RFC doc updated at https://docs.internal/rfcs/service-authz-split (version 0.2).
